headline: The 5 PM HRRR drops its Wednesday-morning burst (0.46 in down to 0.03 in in 3 hours); all models now show light rain late Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, the rating card stays at none, and the king tides are the bigger story.

summary.text: HRRR's 0.46 in burst for 1 to 4 AM Wednesday is gone: the 5 PM run's wettest 3 hours is 0.03 in. NBM and ECMWF nudged up but stay light.
Wettest 3 hours: NBM 0.13 in, ECMWF 0.08, HRRR 0.03 (GFS copies it), RRFS 0.02. Storm totals 0.02 to 0.21 in, well below NWS's 0.5 to 1 in Peninsula range.
Rating card consensus 0.035 in: no street flooding expected. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour, roughly five times the wettest model.
Dry through Tuesday afternoon. Light rain from late Tuesday evening, steadiest about 1 to 5 AM Wednesday, ending by mid-morning. Thanksgiving dry; more rain likely this weekend.
The light rain overlaps the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday, running about 8.4 ft with surge. Late-morning king tides run about 10.8 ft Tuesday and Wednesday. Channel low: 0.14 ft at 7 PM.
Before Tuesday evening: clear street drain grates and yard drains. Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday: gusts can cut power to the pumps. Stay off the Bay shore at the late-morning high tides.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Dry tonight. A cold front tied to an intense low off the Pacific Northwest crosses the Bay Area Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. NWS San Francisco (key messages updated 12:39 PM, discussion issued 3:53 PM) says the moisture plume runs south to north, keeping the heaviest rain to our north, and still lists 0.5 to 1 in for the San Mateo Peninsula and Santa Cruz Mountains. Gusts 25 to 35 mph Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning, up to 45 mph near the Bays. Isolated thunderstorms are possible over the coastal waters and North Bay, and the abnormally warm coastal water could support a strong cell with a localized heavy downpour. Thanksgiving and Friday dry; another storm likely this weekend into early next week. The Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines runs to 4 PM Thursday; NWS calls it major to extreme coastal flooding this week.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
The main change since the 1:25 PM discussion: the new HRRR (5 PM run) no longer has the 0.26 in hour and 0.46 in 3-hour burst it showed for 1 to 4 AM Wednesday. It now has only two light hours, 0.016 in at midnight and 0.028 in at 7 AM Wednesday. The 11 AM burst was not supported by any other model and has not come back.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 7 PM Monday to 7 PM Thursday:
• HRRR (5 PM Mon run, extended to 4 PM Wed): 0.03 / 0.04 in. Down from 0.46 / 0.58 in.
• RRFS (10 AM Mon run, newer than last time): 0.02 / 0.02 in, all of it 4 to 5 AM Wednesday. Little changed (0.02 / 0.04 in).
• NBM: 0.13 / 0.21 in, wettest 1 to 4 AM Wednesday, about 0.05 in per hour at its peak. Up from 0.07 / 0.14 in.
• ECMWF: 0.08 / 0.17 in, about 0.01 in per hour from 8 PM Tuesday, then 0.03 in per hour 2 to 5 AM Wednesday. Up from 0.02 / 0.04 in.
• GFS: again identical to HRRR hour for hour, so no independent information.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Tuesday): first rain 0.004 in per 15 minutes from 11:15 PM Tuesday.

Consensus (HRRR 0.03 × 1.25 = 0.035, RRFS 0.02, NBM 0.13): middle value 0.035 in, down from 0.07 in, so the rating card stays at none. The models now agree on a light, steady frontal rain rather than a burst. NWS's Peninsula total of 0.5 to 1 in is still well above every model, so the consensus may be low on the total, but even the wettest model's hardest hour (NBM 0.05 in) is far below the 0.40 in one-hour Yellow trigger.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (now running to 1 PM Wednesday) is about 1.2 to 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City and about 0.9 to 1.6 ft above the lows. Tonight's 7.0 ft high at 12:16 AM Tuesday runs about 8.3 ft. Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM runs about 10.8 ft. Tuesday evening's -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM runs about -0.3 ft, an easy time for the channel to drain.

The light rain early Wednesday overlaps the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM: the model has 8.2 ft at 1 AM, 8.4 ft at 2 AM, 7.7 ft at 3 AM, 6.5 ft at 4 AM and 5.2 ft at 5 AM, so the channel drains slowly in the steadiest rain and better after about 4 AM. With rain rates near 0.05 in per hour or less, that should not matter much on the street. New this time: the model now covers Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM, running about 10.8 ft, after the rain has ended.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge, highs 2.4 ft above normal Tuesday, 2.7 ft Wednesday and 2.2 ft Thursday including up to 1.5 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there; up to 2.7 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.14 ft at 7 PM, flat between 0.12 and 0.14 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM, its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry on the street. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to 5:13 PM. NWS expects VFR conditions and high clouds until rain moves in with the front Tuesday, with southeast winds increasing ahead of it.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Tuesday afternoon: dry. For Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, the models have converged on light rain, which lowers the street-flooding risk. Two things keep some uncertainty: NWS still forecasts 0.5 to 1 in for the Peninsula, several times any model's total, and a strong cell off the warm coastal water could briefly exceed every model, as HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts here by about 3×. Even tripling the wettest model's 3-hour amount (0.13 in) stays well under the 0.71 in Yellow threshold. The more certain hazard this week is tidal flooding along the Bay shore at the late-morning high tides.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Tuesday before evening: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains; check sandbags.
• Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning: gusts 25 to 35 mph, up to 45 mph near the Bay; outages can slow the pumps.
• Tuesday night: no need to move cars on current guidance; if a heavy downpour does develop, move them out of the cul-de-sac and take timestamped photos.
• Stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads at the late-morning high tides through Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
